calls.thesis: Stance flips from HOLD (2 Nov): cheapest name on the list at 0.24x price-to-sales with 146% upside at 0.6x sales on $77.6bn revenue (+98%); makes the best high-performance servers of the three server makers — but management scandals and -$6.9bn free cash flow are the reason it is cheap.
calls.base_case: At 0.6x sales on $77.6bn revenue, ~146% upside to a $46.5bn market cap.
calls.bull_case: Management stays out of the way, data-centre spend continues and the multiple reaches 0.7x sales or more.
calls.bear_case: Another management scandal or the revenue wall (11% growth next year) keeps investors away.

calls.thesis: Still holds 27,000 shares, all covered by calls struck $35-$40, up ~15% on the position with ~$130,000 of premium downside protection. Pre-announced fiscal Q1 revenue up to $19.5B vs $15.5B guidance and margins near 12.5% vs under 11% expected; at 7x expected $4.67 EPS the valuation looks attractive again if the AI sell-off does not become a bear market, with $45-$50 possible over the next year.
calls.price_at_call: $45-$50 over the next year (average analyst target just over $40); covered calls $35-$40

calls.thesis: Looking to close out the whole position: ~27,000 shares, covered calls at $35-$40 expiring in January, and he will exit when it rebounds to $40-$45 (he still thinks $40-$45/$50 is reachable on valuation and its AI server position). Tired of the volatility and management/accounting problems; still up ~$93k plus covered-call income.
calls.price_at_call: Recently rallied past $45; exit zone $40-$45; covered calls struck $35-$40
